claim.claim-text: 2. The fuel burner (340) of claim 1, wherein the fluid directing structure (352) on the inner tube (344) includes a plurality of openings and a guide associated with each opening, the guides being angled relative to the inner surface for radially rotating the pre-mixed mixture about the central axis (341).
3. The fuel burner (340) of claim 2, wherein the guides are arranged in a series of rows that extend continuously around the periphery of the inner tube (344) to encircle the central axis (341).

4. The fuel burner (340) of claim 2, wherein the fluid directing structure (348) on the outer tube (342) includes a plurality of openings and a guide associated with each opening, the guides being angled relative to the inner surface for radially rotating the pre-mixed mixture about the central axis (341).
5. The fuel burner (340) of claim 4, wherein the guides are arranged in a series of rows that extend continuously around the periphery of the inner tube (344) to encircle the central axis (341).

6. The fuel burner (340) of claim 1, wherein the fluid directing structure (352) on the inner tube (344) extends around the entire periphery of the inner tube (344) such that a flame envelope overlies and intermixes with the pre-mixed mixture entering the fluid passage from the fluid directing structure (348) on the outer tube (342).
7. The fuel burner (340) of claim 1, wherein the pre-mixed mixture is radially layered within the fluid passage.
8. The fuel burner (340) of claim 1, wherein the fuel burner (340) produces about 10ppm of total NO<x> at about 10% CO<2>.
9. A heating appliance including the fuel burner (340) of claim 1.

10. The fuel burner of claim 1 further comprising a housing (380) defining an interior for receiving the inner tube (344) and the outer tube (342), the a plate securing the second end (347) of the outer tube (342) to the housing (380) in a fluid-tight manner.

11. The fuel burner (340) of claim 1, wherein the second end wall (390) is movable along the central axis (341) relative to the inner tube (344) and the outer tube (342) for varying the volume of the fluid passage that receives the pre-mixed mixture.
